decisive_items: a left periprosthetic soft-tissue mass measuring 9 × 8 × 10 cm, without bony involvement or bone-marrow edema
Serum cobalt and chromium levels were within normal limits
response.rationale: The large periprosthetic soft-tissue mass without bone involvement, normal serum cobalt/chromium, and negative cultures favor an adverse local tissue reaction over metallosis, osteolysis, or infection. Chronic infection is the closest alternative given the elevated synovial WBC and CRP, but negative cultures and normal ESR make it less likely; the initial bursitis and partial steroid response do not explain progressive radicular pain and restricted motion.

rejected.why: Isolated bursitis cannot explain the large mass, progressive neurologic symptoms, and restricted hip motion.
Normal serum cobalt and chromium and a ceramic-on-ceramic bearing make metal-wear metallosis unlikely.
No bony involvement and unchanged radiographs argue against osteolysis.
Infection is less likely than ALTR because cultures were negative and there were no systemic signs; elevated synovial WBC can occur in ALTR.
Tendinosis does not account for the periprosthetic mass or radicular symptoms.
